title: librarian-contradiction-invalidation
intention: The librarian detects and invalidates contradicted or stale facts before they are retrieved — the field survey's sharpest production-failure finding.
why: The field survey's sharpest finding: production failures are dominated by stale/contradicted/wrongly-retained facts, NOT recall failures — yet benchmarks test recall only. Measured: 97.8% of 10,134 Mem0 entries junk after 32 days; benchmark-91.6% collapsing to ~49% effective at 38% staleness (arXiv 2606.15903). The tenure loop handles corroboration and neglect but not wrongness — a node promoted to 'earned' that later becomes false has no downward path except waiting 14 days for decay, and decay exempts corroborated nodes. The lived symptom: the librarian confidently repeats something that was true last week.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured: stale/contradicted knowledge is an unmeasured claim still treated as known
Law 7 — errors loud and permanent: a contradicted fact that stays retrievable is a silent error

falsifier.proves_green: A deposit-time contradiction detector that scans near-topic existing nodes, confirms contradiction via inference, and calls refute() on the contradicted node. Proof teeth: (1) depositing a statement that contradicts an existing earned node with source='correction' refutes the existing node — standing changes to 'refuted'; (2) depositing a statement that contradicts an existing hypothesis refutes it — refute() handles hypothesis-vs-hypothesis; (3) depositing a statement near-topic but NOT contradictory does not refute anything — inference confirmation gates the refute call; (4) the contradicted node is NOT deleted — standing='refuted' and provenance carries the refutation attestation (invalidate-don't-delete); (5) _label_evidence() excludes the refuted node from resolution walks; (6) the refuter's provenance carries a 'contradicts' field naming the contradicted node_id.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a contradicted earned node still appears in resolution walks at its former standing; (2) the contradicting deposit does not record WHAT it contradicts (no provenance link); (3) the invalidated node is deleted rather than marked (history lost); (4) invalidation fires on structure alone (cosine similarity) without an inference step confirming actual contradiction — near-topic is not contradiction; (5) a self-contradicting deposit within the same crossing invalidates itself (same-crossing honesty still holds).

how.detection: Deposit-time contradiction scan. When deposit() writes a new node (not a duplicate), run a contradiction check against the k nearest existing nodes (k=5, using the same cosine walk the loop already does). The cheap filter is cosine — only near-topic nodes are candidates for contradiction. The confirming step is an inference call (resolve with kind='generate') that judges: 'Does statement A contradict statement B?' with a binary answer. This is the field's best-performing approach (deposit-time, ~2.3s/case bounded by k neighbors).
how.mechanism: When inference confirms contradiction: (1) The contradicting deposit has ALREADY landed normally (it IS a new node with its own provenance). (2) Call existing refute() on the contradicted node, with the new node_id as refuter_id and the inference judgment as evidence. refute() already handles: the standing gate (_may_retire_earned — a hypothesis cannot retire an earned node unless it's a correction), the crossing-honesty check, and the provenance append. (3) Add a 'contradicts' field to the new node's provenance linking to the contradicted node_id — the relationship is traceable from BOTH sides (refuted node's attestations name the refuter; refuter's provenance names what it replaced).
how.standing_interaction: Fully rides existing physics. refute() sets standing='refuted'. _label_evidence() already excludes refuted nodes (first check, above earned pass-through — the order IS the correctness). _may_retire_earned() already gates hypothesis-vs-earned. A new 'invalidated' standing is NOT needed — 'refuted' is the standing, and the provenance attestation distinguishes machine-detected contradiction from explicit refutation by the evidence field content.
how.integration_point: A new function contradiction_scan(node_id, vector, conn) called from LibrarianDevice.deposit() AFTER the successful deposit write. The scan is a post-write side effect — the deposit is never held pending on it (the node lands regardless; contradiction modifies standing of EXISTING nodes, not the incoming one). If the inference call fails, the contradiction goes undetected — a missed detection, not a data loss — and the node stands on its own merits through the tenure loop.
how.re_validation: An invalidated (refuted) node CAN be re-validated by later evidence. The path: a new deposit arrives that RE-STATES the contradicted claim. The content-hash dedup means it appends an attestation to the EXISTING refuted node. A separate re-validation function (or a future extension of corroborate) could restore standing from 'refuted' to 'hypothesis' when a refuted node receives N new attestations — but this is OUT OF SCOPE for this ticket; the path exists structurally, the trigger is future work.
how.cost_bound: One cosine walk (read, no inference) + at most k inference calls per deposit, where k is the number of near-topic neighbors that pass the cosine threshold. In practice most deposits contradict nothing — the expensive path is rare. The cosine threshold for 'near enough to be a contradiction candidate' is a dial (start at 0.7, same neighborhood as RESOLUTION_FLOOR).
